comment:
This comment covers the same change in several sections/text/illustrations:

Emphasize the use of WHO products throughout the full document so that references to the WHO standards precede references to non-WHO terminologies by the wording. This will enhance usability of guidance to all global users, obtaining equity by including LMICs. General suggestion for alteration: suggested alteration "WHO-standards and terminologies like (WHO-FIC and ICD, ATC, ICD-O and more), with the addition of […]when relevant"

Identified areas for adjustment:

1. Section 3.6.2 – line 812-814: ; SNOMED CT (and SNOMED GPS), ICD-11 and LOINC for clinical terminology and classification

2. Table in Product registry, Appendix C, just above line 502 by the box " Relevant standards". This table box needs som tidying, and misses mentioning that ICD cover more than clinical indications, and the mentioneing of ATC and ICHI 

3.  Section 4.5.2 - line 505-506:   …(for example to SNOMED CT/GPS, ICD-11 and LOINC)

4. Figure 3.3 and 3.5) DHI-H Reference Architecture Integrated wiew, under interoperability and open standards, terminology. 

5. Figure 3.4.3 NHDD Framework: Content Structure, upper box.

public.suggestedRevision:
Refer to numbered bullet point above, and exchange text as followed:

1. Suggested change:
"The architecture references, rather than reinvents, established and openly governed standards, among them HL7 FHIR for the exchange-oriented representation of health data; WHO reference classifications ICD, ICF and ICHI and ICD-O for clinical terminology and classification; additionally SNOMED CT (and SNOMED GPS), and LOINC [...]"

2. Suggest change: WHO-standards and terminologies like (WHO-FIC and ICD, ICHI, ICD-O and more), with the addition of SNOMED CT/GPS ), HL7 FHIR Medication and 
Medication […]when relevant"

3. Suggested change: Terminology and semantic specialists, who curate value sets, code systems, and mappings (for example  WHO-standards and terminologies like WHO-FIC and ICD, ATC, ICD-O and more, with the addition of SNOMED CT and LOINC when relevant) and operate the 
semantic governance processes. 

4. Suggested change: "(WHO-FIC and ICD, SNOMED CT, LOINC)"

5.Suggested change: "Reference / Administrative Code Sets (e.g. WHO-FIC/ICD/ICF/ICHI, ATC, SNOMED CT, LOINC).
